To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plants respond differently to abiotic stresses and that the photosynthetic machinery is a key target for the regulation of plant metabolism and survival in a stressful environment.

abiotic stress causes a decrease in the expression of genes related to the photosynthesis and photosynthetic proteins, especially, in chloroplasts and mitochondria, and this leads to a decrease in the photosynthetic efficiency of plants.
the photosynthesis-related genes and proteins are regulated in response to abiotics stresses and this regulation is a key for plant survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of abiotic stress response in plants, and the regulation of photosynthetic pathways in plants under abiotic stress conditions.
the molecular and biochemical mechanisms that are involved in the regulation and expression of photosynthetic genes in plants under abiotic stresses.
the effects of abiotic stress (drought, salt, and cold) on the photosynthetic system and photosynthetic proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plants are able to adapt and respond to the stress by a coordinated expression of nuclear and chloroplast-encoded photosynthesis-related genes.
abiotic stress causes a reduction in photosynthesis by altering the gene expression and protein profile in photosynthetic systems of plants.
abiotic stress induces the expression of photosynthesis-related genes and proteins, and these proteins are the key players in the photosynthetic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the abiotic stresses cause the alteration in photosynthetic components and pathways.
the plant response and adaptation to abiotic stress are complex and dynamic, and are affected by several factors.
photosynthetic systems are affected by abiotic stresses and the photosynthetic systems of different plants react differently to the same stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plant photosynthetic system has a complex network of regulation that can be exploited for the improvement of plant tolerance against abiotic stresses.
the abiotic stress affects the photosynthesis of plants in a complex manner.
the plant photosynthetic system is the most important target of abiotic stress.
